title: Iff-split of IMO 1959 P2(a): IsGood x (sqrt 2) iff x in [1/2, 1]
intent: Prove part (a) of IMO 1959 P2 — the real x with IsGood x (sqrt 2) are exactly the interval [1/2, 1] — by splitting the iff into its two directions with refine ⟨_, _⟩. Both directions were already packaged as named lemmas: the forward direction reuses IsGood.one_half_le for the lower bound and IsGood.sqrt_two_lt_of_one_lt for the upper bound, and the reverse direction reuses isGood_iff_eq_sqrt_two, so the 3-line glue is pure assembly.

parent.name: imo1959_p2a
parent.statement: problem imo1959_p2a : IsGood x (sqrt 2) ↔ x ∈ solution_set_sqrt2

children.name: IsGood.one_half_le
children.statement: theorem IsGood.one_half_le (h : IsGood x A) : 1 / 2 ≤ x

children.name: isGood_iff_eq_sqrt_two
children.statement: theorem isGood_iff_eq_sqrt_two (hx : x ∈ Icc (1 / 2) 1) : IsGood x A ↔ A = sqrt 2
children.closed_by: suffices 2 = A * sqrt 2 ↔ A = sqrt 2 by convert this using 2; ring, then rw [← div_eq_iff, div_sqrt, eq_comm]; positivity

children.name: IsGood.sqrt_two_lt_of_one_lt
children.statement: theorem IsGood.sqrt_two_lt_of_one_lt (h : IsGood x A) (hx : 1 < x) : sqrt 2 < A
children.closed_by: rw [(isGood_iff_eq_sqrt hx).1 h]; refine sqrt_lt_sqrt zero_le_two ?_; linarith

applicability.goal_shape: A goal of the form P ↔ Q where Q is a membership in a set (here x ∈ solution_set_sqrt2, which unfolds to the interval Icc (1 / 2) 1), and P is a predicate with several conjuncts of well-definedness plus an equation (here IsGood x (sqrt 2)). Both directions of the equivalence have already been stated as named lemmas in the same file.
applicability.use_when: both directions of the equivalence are already packaged as named lemmas, so the iff-split reduces to citing them; the two directions want different lemmas (here a pair of consequences for the forward direction, a single characterisation for the reverse).
applicability.avoid_when: the directions are not yet lemma-sized and need new arguments written inline (then the subgoals are the real content, as in the tactic-scale version); one direction is definitional or follows by symmetry; or the same hypothesis has to be reproved for each direction.

consequences: The split creates exactly two obligations, one per implication; here each is closed by citing named lemmas, so the glue carries no new proof burden. The forward direction must discharge two membership conditions (the lower and upper bounds of the interval Icc (1 / 2) 1), which is why it cites two lemmas (IsGood.one_half_le, IsGood.sqrt_two_lt_of_one_lt) while the reverse cites one (isGood_iff_eq_sqrt_two). Failure mode: if those lemmas were not already available, the 3-line glue would have to grow their sub-proofs inline, defeating the theorem-scale assembly.
